prompt:
A single continuous photograph of one room: a colonial governor's study
in the Caribbean in the 1660s, seen from the doorway. A stern governor
in period dress, a long dark wig, a brocade coat with lace cravat, sits
behind a heavy carved wooden desk with papers, a quill and a brass
candlestick, placed in the left third of the picture. The candle on the
desk is the only light: it lights the governor warmly, and the same
wood-panelled wall continues to the right, fading gradually into deep
shadow, plain and empty, filling the right half of the picture.
Historical reenactment photography, 35mm lens, natural textures, sharp
focus, realistic. Style: one consistent look for the whole series, photographed like a
period film still of the 1660s Caribbean, natural warm light, gentle
film grain, muted rich colours with warm amber and deep teal tones,
moderate contrast, shallow depth of field, realistic textures, no text.
